titulo: Medicines you took years ago may still be changing your gut 🦠
descripcion: A study of 2,509 people in the Estonian Biobank found that many medications leave changes in gut bacteria that can still be seen years later. Never stop a treatment without talking to your doctor. Sources below 👇

escenas.texto: A medicine you took years ago may still be shaping the bacteria in your gut today.
Scientists in Estonia looked at the stool samples and prescription records of two thousand five hundred and nine people.
Out of one hundred and eighty six drugs, one hundred and sixty seven were linked to changes in gut bacteria. Almost nine in ten.
And not just antibiotics. Antidepressants, beta blockers, acid reducers and anti-anxiety drugs too. For several, the change was still there years after people stopped.

visual.sub: other drugs leave a mark too

escenas.texto: So what should you do? First: never stop a treatment on your own. Talk to your doctor.
Second: antibiotics don't work on colds or the flu, because those are viruses. Take them only when a doctor prescribes them, and finish them.
Save this for the next time someone offers you antibiotics for a cold. Follow for more science, with sources.
